regulator files by hand
slides.lead: When a passenger escalates to AESA, you have thirty days to answer with evidence. Cura assembles that file, recommends whether to defend or pay, and learns from every ruling so the next case is argued better.

slides.title: What a single escalation costs you

stats.text: days to respond, from the moment AESA writes
separate items of evidence typically requested
systems a specialist has to search by hand

slides.body: Hours of specialist or legal time, against a deadline, on a claim worth a few hundred euros. Miss the deadline and the authority decides on the record as it stands.

slides.title: This work sits between your systems

byhand.title: A person, by hand
byhand.text: Every case · 30-day deadline · from €250 at stake

slides.body: No system owns this work, because it sits between all of them.

steps.title: Request in
steps.detail: The authority's email arrives from your mailbox or your CRM. Stored raw, before anything reads it.

steps.title: Read & match
steps.detail: AI reads the request and works out which booking, flight and claim it concerns. Low confidence goes to a person.

steps.title: Gather
steps.detail: Four sources, called in parallel. A source that fails marks a gap and the run continues.

steps.title: Compute facts
steps.detail: Versioned code, no AI. Same inputs produce the same number every time — which is what makes it defensible.

steps.title: Draft
steps.detail: AI writes the prose from the computed facts. It never produces a number, a date or a citation of its own.

steps.title: Approve
steps.detail: Your agent reviews, edits and approves. Every change is recorded against the draft, with their name on it.

stats.text: rotation legs traced back to Orly

slides.body: The aircraft arrived into Barcelona 171 minutes late that morning, having overnighted at Palma after arriving 18 minutes late from Paris — so the cause began that morning, and that is exactly the question a regulator would press.

items.text: — the first two items AESA asks for. Without them there is no filing.

slides.body: This is the longest lead time in the project and it is unaffected by anything else. We would rather raise it in the first meeting than the third.

cards.title: Weeks 1–6
cards.text: One real escalation, end to end. Compared against the same case assembled by hand — hours and quality, side by side.

cards.title: Weeks 6–12
cards.text: Your team reviews and files live cases in the screen. Go or no-go on the basis of what they think of it.

cards.title: After
cards.text: Automated intake, filing, outcome capture. The learning loop begins accumulating.

slides.quote: Where the file assembles itself, tells your agent whether to defend or pay, and argues a little better every time a ruling comes back.
